newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Russia set to break De Beers deadline.
newsitem.headline: Russia set to break De Beers deadline.

text.p: A New Year's Eve deadline for Russia to sign a new trade deal with diamond giant De Beers is looming and almost certain to be broken, the South African firm said on Monday.
De Beers has given the Russian government until the end of 1996 to approve a draft agreement on diamond exports or face termination of an interim accord.
A De Beers spokesman said that it was unlikely there would be any movement from Russia before the deadline and so the interim agreement was set to end.
"It is looking unlikely given that there is only 24 hours to go...De Beers will become a buyer of Russian diamonds on a willing buyer, willing seller basis," he said.
But the spokesman added that the breakdown would hopefully only last a short time as Russia has indicated its willingness to sign a deal in 1997.
"De Beers is still hopeful that the deal will be signed," he said.
On Friday Russian Finance Minister Alexander Livshits said that Moscow believed a deal with De Beers was "essential" and could be signed next year, Itar-Tass news agency said.

De Beers controls about three quarters of the world diamond market and Russia accounts for about 25 percent of all rough gems De Beers sells. A five-year deal expired in December 1995 and was replaced by a memorandum signed in February 1996.
De Beers set the end-of-year deadline after being frustrated over Moscow's lack of response on the new trade deal and irritated by gem exports outside the interim scheme.

Despite the deadline's likely expiry Russia's diamond company Almazy Rossii-Sakha, or ARS, which is De Beers' negotiating partner and Russia's near-monopoly producer, has said Moscow would eventually negotiate a deal and quitting the cartel is not an option.
